sources: Field check per locale: official immigration and embassy pages, climate normals, IQAir/EEA air data, rental listings and cost indices, safety advisories; linked on each locale
method: Months are scored from Meridian data (Comfort Index, seasonal hazards, tourist seasons). The field check's month ratings ride along unscored; its nine anchored scores give an overall that ranks locales within their role (ADR 0024).

locales.name: Chiang Mai
locales.summary: Chiang Mai is still the easiest place in Asia to settle in for months: fibre, coworking, mountain cafes and Thai food at very low cost, with a large long-stay community. Plan around burning season (roughly mid-February to April), when PM2.5 reaches hazardous levels; be elsewhere then.

monthNotes.reason: cool and dry: normals show 25 C and 22 C means with 30 mm and 10 mm of rain; clear air; peak-season prices
coolest month (22 C mean, 11 mm rain) but smoke starts to build late in the month
burning season: AQI 170 on 25 Mar 2025, a top-10 most polluted city ranking in April 2026; Apr is the hottest month at a 29.6 C mean
rainy season, 127-216 mm a month (Aug peak 216 mm), humid and 27-29 C means; green, cheap, air clean
rain easing to 124 mm and air clean, 26.6 C mean; some flooding risk early in the month

stay.why: Best used as a Nov-Jan base; move out before smoke builds in mid-February. A DTV covers 180 days per entry.

cost.note: furnished 1-bed in Nimman/Old City, food, transport, coworking; insurance excluded

entry.summary: Visa-exempt stay for US, UK and most EU passports is 30 days since 15 Sep 2026 (the 60-day scheme ended; land-border use is generally capped at twice per calendar year). Destination Thailand Visa (DTV): 5-year multiple entry, up to 180 days per entry, one 180-day extension at an immigration office (about 1,900 THB), fee about 10,000 THB, age 20+, about 500,000 THB in savings held for 3 months, remote work for foreign clients only. Since 31 Aug 2026 applicants must also submit proof of permanent residence and a criminal-record clearance certificate. Tourist visa (60 days plus one 30-day extension) is the fallback. Tax: staying 180 days or more in a calendar year makes you a Thai tax resident, and foreign-sourced income earned from 2024 onward is taxable when brought into Thailand, in the year earned or any later year (Revenue Dept orders Por. 161/2566 and 162/2566).

events.name: Yi Peng and Loy Krathong lantern festivals

locales.caveats: Thai visa rules changed in late 2026 (30-day exemption from 15 Sep; DTV document changes from 31 Aug) and guides differ on DTV financial-proof wording; the 500,000 THB figure comes from a single guide, so confirm on thaievisa.go.th and with the embassy handling your application. Safety rests on Numbeo perception data and internet on Speedtest country medians, neither city-specific for broadband reliability. Month ratings treat February as avoid because late-February smoke is usually hazardous; no monthly PM2.5 means were found. Health: two JCI hospitals in the city (Chiang Mai Ram, Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai).

locales.name: Da Nang / Hoi An
locales.area: Da Nang with Hoi An 30 km south; Hoi An is not in the city data
locales.summary: Da Nang pairs a long city beach and cheap, excellent street food with the old town of Hoi An 30 km away, and a solid nomad scene. Its drawbacks are a typhoon and flood season from September to November and no remote-work visa: the 90-day e-visa cannot be extended in-country.

monthNotes.reason: driest and calmest window: 25-30 C highs, 32-35 mm rain a month, about 7 hours of sun a day
hot (32 C) and getting humid but still low rain, about 57 mm
33 C highs with very high humidity and 18-22 rain days a month; no typhoon peak yet
typhoon and flood peak: Oct averages about 530 mm (Nov about 370 mm), Hoi An floods
cool, grey and drizzly at 24-25 C highs; Dec still wet at about 210 mm

stay.why: 90-day e-visa is the ceiling and is not extendable in-country; best slotted into Feb-May.

cost.note: furnished 1-bed near My Khe beach, food, scooter or Grab, coworking; insurance excluded

entry.summary: No nomad or remote-work visa. E-visa for all nationalities: up to 90 days, single or multiple entry (US$25 / US$50 government fee), generally not extendable inside Vietnam, so a longer stay means exiting and re-applying. Working remotely on a tourist e-visa is a legal grey area. Separately, passports of 13 countries including the UK, Germany and France have a 45-day visa-free entry (Resolution 128); check your passport against the current list and its expiry before relying on it.

events.name: Tet (Lunar New Year) - many businesses close for a week

locales.caveats: Rainfall figures differ between climate datasets (Oct about 455-528 mm); the table here is weather2travel. Da Nang PM2.5 of 14.9 ug/m3 (2025) is IQAir's figure as reported by VnExpress, from only a few stations. No JCI-accredited hospital was found in Da Nang (Hoan My is ACHSI-accredited; Vinmec Da Nang is not one of Vinmec's two JCI hospitals), so serious cases go to Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City or abroad. Safety is Numbeo perception data (54 contributors); internet is the Speedtest country median. Tet date moves between late January and mid-February.

locales.name: Bali
locales.area: Canggu for the scene, Ubud for the spiritual, Amed (north coast, drier) for diving and quiet; Denpasar stands in for the island
locales.summary: Bali has the most developed nomad ecosystem in Asia: coworking, villas, wellness and surf, with Canggu, Ubud and Uluwatu each offering a different pace. Traffic, wet-season downpours and a patchy legal route for long stays are the trade-offs; the E33G visa needs about US$60,000 a year in foreign income.

monthNotes.reason: dry season: Denpasar normals 28-95 mm a month in Jun-Oct and 95 mm in May, sunny with lower humidity
mostly dry (Jul-Aug 28-36 mm) but Jul-Aug are peak crowds and prices; Apr (107 mm) and Nov (131 mm) are transitional with showers
wet season tail, 231 mm; Nyepi usually falls in March and shuts the island and airport for 24 hours
wet-season peak: Dec 327 mm, Jan 351 mm, Feb 290 mm at the airport, with flooding and landslide risk in Canggu and Ubud

stay.why: Visa-on-arrival gives 30 days plus one extension; the E33G is the route for a longer stay but triggers tax-residency questions.

cost.note: furnished 1-bed or villa room in Canggu/Ubud, food, scooter, coworking; insurance excluded

entry.summary: E33G Remote Worker visa (KITAS): 1 year, needs about US$60,000 a year in income from an employer or clients abroad plus savings proof (US$2,000 bank balance for 3 months), no work for Indonesian entities; fees reported as IDR 2.7M (Fragomen, 2024) versus roughly IDR 7M plus add-ons (2026 guide), and renewal reported both as one extra year and as re-applying from abroad. Alternative: 30-day visa on arrival (IDR 500,000 plus fees) extendable once at an immigration office; the arrival card must be filed within 72 hours before entry. Tourist levy IDR 150,000 once per visit. Tax: more than 183 days in 12 months makes you an Indonesian tax resident on worldwide income, and KITAS holders may be treated as resident from day one.

events.name: Nyepi (Day of Silence), island and airport shut for 24 hours

locales.caveats: Sources conflict on E33G fees and renewal, and the tax rules for KITAS holders come from one 2026 guide; confirm with immigration and a tax adviser. Denpasar's 2025 annual PM2.5 was not published in sources I could open: live readings were 22-31 ug/m3 in Nov 2026 and Indonesia's 2025 mean was 30 ug/m3, so the air score assumes about 20 ug/m3. Safety is Numbeo perception data (93 contributors, last updated Oct 2025; night-time walking 46). Internet is the Speedtest country median (fixed 89 Mbps), and villa fibre and Starlink are usually better than that. Only Siloam Bali holds JCI; BIMC Nusa Dua holds ACHSI, and serious cases are commonly evacuated to Singapore.

locales.name: Bangkok
locales.summary: Bangkok is the region's transit hub: top private hospitals, gigabit fibre, excellent food at every price and flights everywhere. Use it for a few days between bases; heat, traffic and seasonal PM2.5 make it a poor place to settle.

monthNotes.reason: rains ending (46 mm), 28.4 C mean, lowest humidity of the year; PM2.5 not yet elevated
dry (13-24 mm) at 27-28 C means, but cool-season PM2.5 episodes begin; annual mean about 23 ug/m3
PM2.5 episodes continue into February, then heat builds toward a 30 C mean in March
hottest month, 30.8 C mean (afternoon highs well above that) with humid heat-index spikes before the rains
rainy season, 183-344 mm a month (Sep 344 mm, Oct 304 mm), near-daily storms and street flooding risk

stay.why: Transit hub: flights, hospitals, visa paperwork; two to ten nights between bases.

cost.note: furnished 1-bed near BTS/MRT, food, transport, coworking; insurance excluded

entry.summary: Visa-exempt stay for US, UK and most EU passports is 30 days since 15 Sep 2026 (the 60-day scheme ended; land-border use is generally capped at twice per calendar year). Destination Thailand Visa (DTV): 5-year multiple entry, up to 180 days per entry, one 180-day extension at an immigration office (about 1,900 THB), fee about 10,000 THB, age 20+, about 500,000 THB in savings held for 3 months, remote work for foreign clients only. Since 31 Aug 2026 applicants must also submit proof of permanent residence and a criminal-record clearance certificate. Tourist visa (60 days plus one 30-day extension) is the fallback. Tax: staying 180 days or more in a calendar year makes you a Thai tax resident, and foreign-sourced income earned from 2024 onward is taxable when brought into Thailand, in the year earned or any later year (Revenue Dept orders Por. 161/2566 and 162/2566).

events.name: Peak flood risk along the river

locales.caveats: Thai visa rules changed in late 2026 (30-day exemption from 15 Sep; DTV document changes from 31 Aug) and guides differ on DTV financial-proof wording; the 500,000 THB figure comes from a single guide, so confirm on thaievisa.go.th and with the embassy handling your application. Safety rests on Numbeo perception data and internet on Speedtest country medians, neither city-specific for broadband reliability. Bangkok's annual PM2.5 (22.7 ug/m3) is from a Smart Air 2025 ranking rather than IQAir city data. Numbeo safety index 62 (night-time walking 58) reflects drug and property-crime concerns.

locales.name: Taipei (+ Hualien/Taitung)
locales.area: Taipei, plus the east coast (Hualien, Taitung) as an add-on
locales.summary: Taipei is one of Asia's easiest big-city bases: very safe, top-tier hospitals, fast fibre, excellent cheap food and a real long-stay route in the Gold Card. The catch is climate: grey and drizzly winters, a hot, humid typhoon-season summer from June to September, and only about four comfortable months (Mar-Apr, Oct-Nov).

monthNotes.reason: highs about 25C, lowest typhoon risk, clearest stretch of the year
18-27C highs; Mar-Apr drizzly (about 14-15 rain days) and Oct can still see a late typhoon
highs 17-20C with grey skies and drizzle on 12-19 days a month (northeast monsoon); no central heating in most flats
plum-rain season, 215-260 mm a month and highs of 29-32C with high humidity
still about 32C and humid, typhoon peak; usually disruptions of a day or two
highs 33-35C with heat index higher, about 250-290 mm rain and the peak of typhoon season

stay.why: 90 days visa-free covers a full autumn or spring stay; longer needs a Gold Card or other visa

cost.note: furnished 1-bed or studio (about NT$25,000-40,000 central, serviced units cost more), food, transit; excludes coworking and insurance

entry.summary: EU, US and UK passports get 90 days visa-free (online arrival card required); no nomad visa exists, and visitor stays are not routinely extended. The Employment Gold Card (open work rights, 1-3 year cards by fee schedule) needs a qualifying field plus a recent average salary of NT$160,000/month before tax (any year in the last three), or other field criteria; fees NT$3,700-5,700 (more for US passports applying abroad). Tax residency begins at 183 days in a calendar year.

events.name: Lantern Festival and Pingxi sky lanterns (date follows lunar calendar, Feb-Mar)
Cherry and azalea bloom around Yangmingshan (Feb-Mar)
Autumn dry spell begins; best hiking weather in Nov

locales.caveats: Monthly ratings use long-term normals from secondary climate sites; they disagree on Taipei's wettest month (June vs August), and Taipei's CWA table was not readable. PM2.5 uses the 2025 national mean (reported as 12.8-13.3 ug/m3, two figures in one article) as a proxy for Taipei. Gold Card salary route confirmed on the official site; reports of a 2026 amendment, a 50% tax break and a USD 6,000 threshold were not confirmed on official pages. The Hualien/Taitung east coast has higher typhoon exposure in Aug-Oct and the April 2024 earthquake damage; not scored separately.

locales.name: Tokyo / Kyoto
locales.summary: Tokyo and Kyoto offer unmatched food, transit, safety and a dense mix of modern and traditional life, and the weather is at its best in April-May and again in October-November. It is costly, and summer is punishing (35C, high humidity, typhoons from late summer), so plan one visit of two to four weeks in a spring or autumn window.

monthNotes.reason: highs 19-24C in Tokyo, light rain; peak crowds late March to early April and Golden Week (29 Apr-5 May)
highs about 18C, dry and clear; koyo foliage peaks late Nov, with heavy Kyoto crowds
highs about 22C, but October is wet (about 200 mm) and typhoons can still arrive
cold highs of 10-14C, dry and sunny; many businesses close around 29 Dec-3 Jan
highs about 13C, cedar-pollen season, sakura crowds and top prices from about 20 Mar
tsuyu rainy season, about 170 mm and high humidity
still about 28C and humid, wettest month (about 220 mm) with peak typhoon risk
highs 31-35C with high humidity; heat-stroke warnings; Kyoto hotter still

stay.why: Enough for both cities and day trips; beyond a month the cost and lack of mid-term rental ease outweigh gains

cost.note: about 2-3 weeks, mid-range hotels or apartments, food, local transport and one Tokyo-Kyoto rail leg; excludes long-haul flights. Cost score is based on a monthly mid-term budget of about EUR 2,500-3,000.

entry.summary: EU, US and UK passports get 90 days visa-free as temporary visitors (no work). The Digital Nomad visa (Designated Activities 53) gives 6 months, not extendable, with annual income at least JPY 10 million, private medical cover of at least JPY 10 million, for about 50 countries; applied for at a Japanese embassy or consulate, and a 6-month wait before reapplying. Visa fees for those who need a visa rose from JPY 3,000 to JPY 15,000 (single entry) on 1 July 2026. The JESTA entry-authorisation law passed in May 2026; start date and fee not yet confirmed. Tax: resident status (and worldwide taxation) generally begins with a domicile or 1 year of residence; 183 days is the usual treaty test.

events.name: Sakura season starts (Tokyo and Kyoto bloom about 25 Mar-5 Apr)
Koyo autumn foliage (peak late Nov in Kyoto and Tokyo)

locales.caveats: Climate and air figures are from long-term normals and general knowledge; I did not pull a Tokyo or Kyoto PM2.5 figure this session (about 9-11 ug/m3 is the commonly reported range). Rating March as fair reflects living conditions, not sightseeing; sakura timing shifts by about a week year to year. JESTA details and Digital Nomad visa fee for 2026 are not confirmed from the Japanese government.

locales.name: Penang (George Town)
locales.area: George Town
locales.summary: George Town is one of the cheapest comfortable bases in Asia: great street food, English widely spoken, good private hospitals, reliable fibre and a formal nomad pass. Weather is hot and humid all year (about 31-33C), with December-February the driest stretch and September-November the wettest, plus occasional haze from Sumatran fires around August-October.

monthNotes.reason: driest and sunniest months, about 70-140 mm rain, but still about 32C and humid
hottest period at 32-34C, humidity high, afternoon storms returning
hot and humid, about 180-230 mm a month, early-morning Sumatras squalls in the southwest monsoon
wet (about 270-370 mm in September) and regional haze episodes, with PM2.5 roughly double the annual mean in September
wettest months, often 300-400 mm, with flash-flood risk and heavy afternoon storms

stay.why: Viable year-round and cheap; the DE Rantau pass supports a full year, though the climate varies little

cost.note: furnished condo (about USD 350-500 in George Town, more in new seafront towers), food, transport, coworking at about USD 80-120; excludes insurance

entry.summary: EU, US and UK passports get 90 days visa-free (online MDAC arrival card required). The DE Rantau Nomad Pass (MDEC) is a 12-month pass, renewable up to three times, for remote workers earning more than USD 24,000/year (tech) or USD 60,000/year (non-tech); the MDEC FAQ v10 shows these figures. Law-firm summaries of an MDEC enhancement, effective 1 Dec 2026, say the tech threshold rises to USD 36,000 (renewals too), the maximum stay becomes 48 months, and new applications pause 1-30 Nov 2026. Tax residency begins at 182 days in a calendar year.

events.name: Chinese New Year (about 6 Feb 2027), many shops shut, busy
George Town Festival (usually Aug) and Hungry Ghost month
Peak haze risk from Sumatran fires (Aug-Oct)
Dry season begins, best weather of the year

locales.caveats: The 1 Dec 2026 DE Rantau changes (USD 36,000 tech threshold, 4-year maximum, a Nov 2026 pause on new applications) come from law-firm and news summaries; the MDEC FAQ v10 that I could read still shows USD 24,000/60,000 and I did not find the primary MDEC notice. Confirm directly with MDEC before applying, especially if applying this week. Monthly rainfall is rounded from secondary climate sites that disagree (annual 2,100-2,500 mm). George Town PM2.5 annual mean was not found; the only figure is about 16 ug/m3 for Balik Pulau (2019), used as an estimate. Safety score reflects snatch theft and motorbike traffic.

locales.name: Goa
locales.area: North (Arambol, Anjuna, Vagator) for the scene, south (Palolem, Agonda) for quiet; Panaji stands in
locales.summary: Portuguese-flavoured Indian coast with a large foreign long-stay scene, cheap rent and a real food, yoga and music community. It only works from November to February; the rest of the year is hot, humid or monsoon-shut, and there is no remote-work visa, only a tourist e-visa with a 180-day yearly cap.

monthNotes.reason: dry, about 32C days and 20-21C nights, humidity near 60%, calm sea; also peak prices
dry and sunny but hotter (32-33C); November still humid, February warming; shacks fully open
33C and 70%+ humidity building, beach shacks start closing in April; quiet
retreating monsoon, thunderstorms and about 200mm rain, humid; shacks only reopening late month
pre-monsoon heat then SW monsoon: June 840mm, July 920mm, rough seas, shacks and many guesthouses closed

stay.why: November-March window; the 180-day calendar-year cap on India e-tourist visas and tax-residency rules limit longer stays

cost.note: furnished 1-bed in Assagao/Anjuna or Palolem, food, scooter, coworking desk; the top of the range is peak December-January rent

entry.summary: No nomad visa; remote work is not authorised on a tourist visa (employment is barred on e-visas). e-Tourist visa: 30 days (non-extendable), 1 year or 5 years multiple-entry; on the 1/5-year visas stays are up to 90 days per visit (reported 180 for US/UK/Canada/Japan) and total stay must not exceed 180 days in a calendar year. Apply 4 to 120 days ahead; fees vary by nationality and season (30-day roughly USD 10-25, 1-year about USD 40). Foreigners must be registered (Form C, usually via the landlord). India's tax-residency test is 182 days in a financial year, so the 180-day cap sits just under it.

events.name: IFFI film festival, Panaji (usually late November)
Christmas and New Year peak season, prices spike
Monsoon onset, seas closed to swimming

locales.caveats: Annual PM2.5 for Goa not found in IQAir results; air score is an estimate (roughly 20 ug/m3, with winter dust and construction spikes in Porvorim/Panaji rated poor on some days). Rent and budget figures come from nomad/listing sites and vary widely; INR conversion approximate. Per-visit 180 days for US/UK is from secondary sources only; the official page states just the 180-day yearly cap. Mopa airport (GOX) also serves north Goa.

locales.name: Sri Lanka south coast (Galle/Mirissa/Weligama)
locales.area: Galle, Mirissa, Weligama
locales.summary: Galle Fort, Weligama and Mirissa give a cheap, social beach base with surf, whales, cafes and coworking, and now a real one-year nomad visa. The dry window is only about December to March, and the south-west monsoon plus the October-November rains make the rest of the year wet; November 2025 showed how severe late-year storms can get.

monthNotes.reason: driest months (about 75-95mm), calm seas, 30C days with sea breeze; peak prices
mostly dry and calm; December about 150mm, March heat building to 30C+ and rain returning
inter-monsoon thunderstorms in April (about 250mm) and November (about 300mm, cyclone risk); Jul-Sep rougher sea, 150-230mm, some places shut
May about 380mm and June about 280mm SW monsoon with rough surf; October about 340mm, wettest month with flood risk

stay.why: Best as a December-March base; the nomad visa allows 12 months but the monsoon months are poor

cost.note: 1-bed guesthouse or apartment (USD 300-800), food, scooter, coworking; excludes insurance and the USD 500 visa fee

entry.summary: Digital Nomad Visa (launched Feb 2026): 1 year, renewable annually, USD 2,000/month foreign-sourced income remitted (+USD 500/month per dependant beyond 2), USD 500 per person per year, needs international health insurance, police clearance, medical and security clearance and a Ministry of Digital Economy recommendation; renewal requires Inland Revenue tax registration; no local employment. Without it: since 25 May 2026 EU/US/UK passport holders (most EU states, UK, USA, Canada, Australia on the list of 40) get a free 30-day double-entry tourist ETA, applied for before travel; extensions beyond 30 days cost a fee and reportedly run in steps to a 270-day maximum. Tax residency: a resident for tax if present 183+ days in a year, so a 270-day tourist stay can trigger it.

events.name: Blue whale and dolphin season off Mirissa (Nov-Apr)
Sinhala and Tamil New Year (mid-April, many shops shut)
SW monsoon peak, red flags on beaches

locales.caveats: No audited PM2.5 figure found for the south coast; air score is an estimate (about 15 ug/m3, coastal). Rent and speeds come from nomad-aggregator sites; Mirissa 4G is often 10-20 Mbps, Weligama coworking can reach 100+ Mbps. Extension fee table for 2026 not confirmed (older chart: USD 60 for 31-90 days, 150 for 91-180, 200 for 181-270); the 270-day cap is from secondary sources and one says six months. Cyclone Ditwah (late Nov 2025) hit mainly the central and eastern districts and Colombo area, with a death toll of several hundred nationally; monitor the Department of Meteorology in Oct-Dec. Some sources give the DNV launch as April 2026 rather than February.

locales.name: Bhutan (Paro/Thimphu/Punakha)
locales.area: Paro, Thimphu, Punakha; book through a licensed operator
locales.summary: A high-Himalayan trip of dzongs, monasteries and walks, with very low crime and clean mountain air, but not a place to base yourself: tourists pay a USD 100 per night fee on top of ground costs and there is no long-stay or work route. Go for 10 to 14 days in March-May or October-November.

monthNotes.reason: dry, clear, 15-22C days in valleys; April rhododendrons, October-November Himalayan views and festivals
mostly dry and clear; March and December still near-freezing nights in Paro, May warming with first showers
January-February cold (Paro lows to -6C, high passes snowy); September is the monsoon tail with landslide delays
monsoon: Paro July about 550mm, landslides, leeches, cloud hides views; fee still due

stay.why: Compact itinerary of Paro, Thimphu, Punakha, Phobjikha; the nightly fee makes longer stays costly

cost.note: 10-14 days, one adult: SDF USD 100 per night, USD 40 visa, operator-arranged guide, car, hotels and meals; 5% tourism GST applies since 2026; excludes flights

entry.summary: Visa required for EU/US/UK passports, USD 40 once, plus Sustainable Development Fee of USD 100 per adult per night (USD 50 for ages 6-11, free under 6), paid in advance via an online application through a licensed Bhutanese operator or the official tourism portal. The 50% SDF discount (standard USD 200) is stated by the Department of Tourism to run to 31 Dec 2029. No nomad visa and no remote-work route; independent travel is not permitted beyond what the operator arranges.

events.name: Paro Tshechu (lunar; 18-22 March 2027, late Mar/Apr other years)

locales.caveats: Sources disagree on how long the SDF discount runs (31 Dec 2029 per the Department of Tourism and most guides; one BBS report says to August 2027) - confirm with your operator. Whether a licensed operator is strictly mandatory for non-Indian tourists is described differently by different sources; budget on booking through one. No Bhutan or Thimphu PM2.5 figure found; air score is an estimate. Festival dates follow the lunar calendar and shift by weeks. Cost range is built from the fixed fees plus typical operator rates and is not an official tariff.

locales.name: Valencia / Málaga
locales.area: Valencia; Málaga shares its windows in your Travel Seasons
locales.summary: A big, flat, bikeable Mediterranean city (Malaga is the warmer-winter alternative) with excellent food, fibre internet, a large nomad scene and a real nomad visa. Winters are mild (highs 16-17 C) rather than warm and July-August are hot and humid; Sep-Oct is flash-flood alert season.

monthNotes.reason: highs 21-27 C (AEMET), 5-9 rain days a month with only 22-39 mm, 234-276 sunshine hours
highs 16-20 C but lows 7-11 C (mean 11.8 C in Jan) and often unheated flats; about 33-48 mm rain; Fallas (15-19 Mar) is loud and crowded
highs 24-28 C but the wettest months (70 mm Sep, 77 mm Oct); red rain alerts in Oct 2024 (771 mm in Turis), Sep 2025 and Oct 2026
highs 30 C, lows 21.5-22 C (hot nights), humidity 67-68%, heatwaves above 35 C possible

stay.why: Very livable most of the year; the nomad visa allows long residence, but plan around July-August heat and autumn storm alerts

cost.note: furnished 1-bed about EUR1,000-1,350 (average about EUR1,150) plus food, transport, utilities and coworking; insurance excluded

entry.summary: Spain telework (digital nomad) visa for people working remotely for non-Spanish companies: income of at least 200% of the monthly minimum wage (EUR2,849 gross/month in 2026), a degree or 3 years' relevant experience, health insurance covering public-system risks, a clean 5-year criminal record and an NIE; Spanish clients limited to 20% of activity. Visa valid 1 year; people already in Spain can obtain a residence permit of up to 3 years. EU citizens need no visa. US and UK passport holders get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen area, shared with other Schengen countries. The EES biometric border system has been fully live since April 2026; ETIAS is not yet in operation and no start date is published (2027 widely reported). Spanish tax residency starts at more than 183 days in a calendar year.

locales.caveats: Air score uses a modelled 2024 city mean of 10.7 ug/m3 (whichcity.eu from EEA grids, confidence B); IQAir's Valencia page gave no annual figure. Rent is from one aggregator (about EUR1,150 average 1-bed, updated Oct 2026), not a primary survey; Malaga was not priced and its air reading (4.4 ug/m3 on the day) is a snapshot. Spain's special flat-tax option for nomad-visa holders was not verified; take tax advice.

locales.name: Madeira (Funchal)
locales.area: South coast: Funchal, Calheta, Câmara de Lobos
locales.summary: A mild-all-year Atlantic island whose south coast has 20-27 C highs in every month, with levada hiking, a safe Funchal and a small nomad community. Winter and autumn bring short rainy spells, August brings wildfire risk, and rents are only moderately cheap.

monthNotes.reason: highs 21-27 C; rain only 0-45 mm and 0.3-4.7 rain days a month (Jul 1.7 mm, Sep 23 mm)
highs 20-25 C but 62-95 mm rain on 5.5-8.6 rain days (Oct-Dec wettest, 80-95 mm); New Year crowds and prices
hottest month (high 26.8 C, 28 days at 25 C+), dry, busiest; the Aug 2024 wildfire burned 8,000+ ha and reached Funchal

stay.why: Weather suits any month; the island is small, so long stays suit people happy with outdoors and a small city

cost.note: idealista Funchal listings show 1-beds from about EUR900-1,100 up to EUR1,850 (premium EUR3,800); plus food, transport and coworking; insurance excluded

entry.summary: Portugal remote-work visa ('D8'/Nomadas Digitais): proof of average monthly income over the last 3 months of at least 4x the minimum wage (EUR3,680/month in 2026, minimum wage EUR920), employment contract or client contracts, tax-residence document, travel insurance and clean criminal record; a temporary-stay visa (up to about 1 year) or a residence visa that converts to a residence permit via AIMA. EU citizens need no visa. US and UK passport holders get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen area, shared with other Schengen countries. The EES biometric border system has been fully live since April 2026; ETIAS is not yet in operation and no start date is published (2027 widely reported). Portuguese tax residency applies after more than 183 days or with a habitual home there.

locales.caveats: Air score uses a modelled 2024 annual mean of 5.5 ug/m3 for Funchal (whichcity.eu, confidence C); IQAir's Funchal page is satellite-modelled and gives no annual figure. Madeira sets its own regional minimum wage; whether a Madeira application uses the national EUR920 for the income test is unclear (raise it with the consulate). Climate figures are the Funchal coast station only; the north and mountains are cooler and wetter. Savings figures such as EUR11,040 seen in guides are not in the official D8 requirements.

locales.name: Canary Islands (Las Palmas, Tenerife, La Palma)

locales.summary: The year-round mild-weather fallback: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria has 19-27 C highs all year, almost no summer rain, fibre internet and the largest nomad scene in the islands, with Tenerife and La Palma for landscape. Rents are lower than the mainland hubs; drawbacks are Saharan dust episodes and island distance.

monthNotes.reason: highs 22-26 C (AEMET, Gran Canaria airport), 0-22 mm rain a month and 0-4 rain days
highs 21-22 C but lows 15-16 C, the year's rain (24-31 mm on 3-4.5 days) and more cloud; winter-sun peak season for visitors
highs 27 C, lows 21-22 C and humidity about 66-68% at the airport station (cooler by about 2-3 C in the city); dry, trade-wind breezes; August holiday prices

entry.summary: Spain telework (digital nomad) visa for people working remotely for non-Spanish companies: income of at least 200% of the monthly minimum wage (EUR2,849 gross/month in 2026), a degree or 3 years' relevant experience, health insurance covering public-system risks, a clean 5-year criminal record and an NIE; Spanish clients limited to 20% of activity. Visa valid 1 year; people already in Spain can obtain a residence permit of up to 3 years. EU citizens need no visa. US and UK passport holders get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen area, shared with other Schengen countries. The EES biometric border system has been fully live since April 2026; ETIAS is not yet in operation and no start date is published (2027 widely reported). The Canaries are in the Schengen area and the same nomad visa applies; the islands use IGIC (7% general rate) rather than mainland VAT, and the 183-day Spanish tax residency rule applies.

Climate is the airport station (about 2-3 C hotter in summer than the seafront; a reanalysis estimate for the city gives highs of 18-24.5 C), so the best/good split between months is a judgement call. The IGIC rate, calima timing and Atlantic Rally were not verified from a source. Rents are listing asking prices, mostly unfurnished or short-let. The north of Tenerife and La Palma are cooler and wetter.

locales.name: Lisbon / Cascais

EU citizens need no visa. US and UK passport holders get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen area, shared with other Schengen countries. The EES biometric border system has been fully live since April 2026; ETIAS is not yet in operation and no start date is published (2027 widely reported). Portuguese tax residency applies after more than 183 days or with a habitual home there; the old NHR regime was replaced by the narrower IFICI, which most nomads do not qualify for.

locales.caveats: Air score uses a modelled 2024 annual mean of 7.9 ug/m3 for Lisbon (whichcity.eu from EEA grids, confidence B). Climate is the Gago Coutinho station (104 m, inland of the centre); Cascais on the coast is cooler in summer. Rent evidence is idealista asking prices for mixed flat sizes, so the cost range is partly judgement; one-bedroom median figures from news sites were not opened. The IFICI and Web Summit dates were not re-verified. Savings figures such as EUR11,040 in guides are not in the official remote-work visa requirements.

locales.name: Montenegro (Kotor/Budva)

Longer stays otherwise need a work/own-company/property-based temporary residence. Tax residency generally starts at 183 days; Montenegro's corporate tax is 9% (low band) and the nomad route requires foreign-sourced income.

Heavy autumn rain around Kotor bay

entry.summary: Not Schengen. UK and EU passport holders: visa-free 90 days in any 180 (UK government advice); longer needs a long-stay visa or a residence/Unique Permit applied for in Albania. US citizens: visa-free up to one year from first entry (US State Department advisory, Aug 2026), resetting only after 90 days out; a residence permit is needed beyond a year. Remote workers use the Unique Permit (combined work and residence, typically 1 year, renewable); secondary sources report an income-tax exemption for the first year. Tax residency is generally 183 days.

locales.caveats: Unique Permit fees, income thresholds and the tax exemption come from commercial guides; official Albanian pages not verified. locales.name: Crete (Chania)

entry.summary: Schengen: US and UK passport holders get 90 days in any 180 visa-free (EU citizens may stay freely and register after 3 months). Secondary sources report that since 5 Feb 2026 (Law 5275/2026) applications must start at a Greek consulate rather than in Greece. Tax residency is generally 183 days; a 50% income-tax relief for new residents (up to 7 years) exists with conditions. Schengen legs count toward 90/180; EES biometric entry/exit registration has run at all Schengen external borders since 10 Apr 2026; ETIAS is not yet in operation (launch slipped, 2027 widely expected).

Rent: Numbeo (25 Nov 2026) and Flatio asking prices differ by ~EUR 400; mid-term furnished listings used. Safety: US advisory Level 1 (petty crime common in tourist areas, demonstrations possible). entry.summary: Visa-free tourist entry for US/EU/UK passports: 90 days, extendable once by 90 more, capped at 180 days per calendar year. No measured PM2.5 was found: the 4.5 air score is an estimate allowing for Saharan dust. Rent figures are from expat guides and Numbeo-derived sites, which disagree widely for Sal. The EASE site notes that from 1 January 2026 visa-on-arrival was suspended for nationals of 96 countries, so other passports must check the list.

locales.name: Nicoya Peninsula
locales.area: Nicoya Peninsula; Liberia is the airport
locales.summary: Pacific-coast surf and wellness towns (Nosara, Santa Teresa, Samara, Tamarindo) with a strong remote-work community, a 12-month nomad visa and a Blue Zone reputation. The dry season (December-March) is excellent, the September-October rains are heavy and some businesses close, and costs, remote logistics and healthcare distance are the main drawbacks.

monthNotes.reason: dry, sunny and breezy with highs near 32 C and almost no rain; peak prices
March is dry but hot (33-34 C highs); July has the veranillo dry spell with brief sun-heavy weeks
April is the hottest month (35 C highs) before rains start in May, then the green season brings afternoon storms; November rains taper but roads stay muddy
rainiest months (about 350-400 mm), flooded roads and river crossings, and many businesses closed

stay.why: Dry season fills a 12-16 week window; the visa allows 12 months but the Sep-Oct rains are a poor time to be on the peninsula

cost.note: 1-bed or small house in Santa Teresa/Nosara/Samara (about USD 800-1,300), imported-food premium, car/ATV, coworking desk about USD 250; insurance excluded

entry.summary: Visa-free tourist entry for US, EU and UK passports: normally 90 days. Remote-worker stay under Law 10008: income of at least USD 3,000 per month (USD 4,000 with family), health insurance, work only for foreign employers or clients; granted for 12 months and extendable once for 12 more. Sources disagree on the presence needed to extend (180 days in one, 80 in another). Foreign-source income is exempt from Costa Rican income tax.

events.name: Veranillo dry spell; Guanacaste Day (25 Jul)

locales.caveats: I could not read the official DGME or TramiteYa pages; visa terms come from commercial and press summaries and the renewal presence requirement conflicts (180 vs 80 days). Annual PM2.5 for the Guanacaste coast was not verified (estimated under 10 ug/m3; sugarcane burning and Saharan dust bring brief spikes). Remote beach towns are 1.5-3 hours from Liberia airport and the nearest major hospitals; internet depends on Starlink or local fibre and drops in storms. Homicide rates have risen nationally, mostly organised crime, while tourist towns see mainly theft.

locales.name: New Zealand South Island (Queenstown/Wanaka)
locales.area: Queenstown, Wanaka, Milford Sound, Fiordland; a car is essential
locales.summary: Queenstown, Wanaka and Fiordland offer alpine lakes, hiking, skiing and very safe, fast-connected towns, with remote work for overseas employers allowed on a visitor visa. It is expensive, summer (December-March) is the sweet spot and books out early, and serious hospital care is a few hours away.

monthNotes.reason: long days and highs of 19-23 C; Great Walks open; peak prices Dec-Feb, quieter and settled in March
highs 15-18 C; April has autumn colour and the Great Walks season ending 30 Apr; October-November bring lupins, wind and the Great Walks reopening from late October
highs 8-13 C, frosts and snow, around 8 hours of daylight in June, Milford Road avalanche closures, and ski-season prices June-September

stay.why: Visa-waiver stay is 3 months (6 for UK passports); cost and distance favour one focused summer visit

cost.note: one person, about 4 weeks: furnished 1-bed in Queenstown/Wanaka (about NZD 490-650 per week off-peak, more in summer and ski season), car hire or campervan, food, a few activities; excludes long-haul flights and insurance

entry.summary: No dedicated nomad visa. US and EU passports enter on an NZeTA for up to 3 months per visit (UK passports up to 6 months); the International Visitor Levy of NZD 100 is paid with the NZeTA. Immigration NZ allows unlimited remote work on a visitor visa (applied for on or after 27 Jan 2025) if it is for an employer or clients outside New Zealand and does not require being physically present for NZ work. Income is generally not taxed in NZ if you stay under 92 days in 12 months (up to 183 days where a tax treaty applies).

events.name: Queenstown Winter Festival and ski season opens

locales.caveats: The immigration page does not say explicitly whether the remote-work allowance covers NZeTA (visa-waiver) travellers as well as visitor-visa holders; confirm with Immigration NZ before relying on it. I could not verify any change to NZ tax rules for visitors in 2026. Rental prices are asking prices, euro conversion assumes roughly NZD 1 = EUR 0.5 and should be rechecked, and summer rents run well above the off-peak listings found. Winter is rated fair rather than avoid because skiing is the main draw; it is a poor fit for a car-free, long working stay.

locales.name: Seoul
locales.summary: Seoul is very safe, superbly connected (gigabit fibre, 24-hour food and transit) and has top-tier hospitals, with real nomad infrastructure in Mapo, Seongsu and Gangnam. April-May and October are excellent; the July-August monsoon and the cold, dry winter (often below -5C at night) are the drawbacks, along with spring dust and a PM2.5 mean around 18 ug/m3.

monthNotes.reason: highs 18-24C, cherry blossom early April, low humidity
highs about 19C, clear dry air and autumn foliage
highs 25-27C; late June starts jangma rains and early September can bring typhoon tails
highs about 12C, dry; foliage fades and it turns cold by month end
dry but cold: January highs near 1C and lows around -6C, with cold snaps lower
highs about 11C, yellow dust and PM2.5 episodes above 35 ug/m3 on some days
jangma monsoon then humid 30C+ heat; July-August bring about 370-390 mm each and flash-flood risk

stay.why: 90 days visa-free covers a spring or autumn base; longer needs the F-1-D visa, which has a high income bar

cost.note: furnished officetel or 1-bed in Mapo/Seongsu/Gangnam, food, transit; excludes coworking and insurance. Short officetel rentals can add deposit, agent and exit fees.

entry.summary: EU, US and UK passports get 90 days visa-free (tourism and short business only); K-ETA is waived until 31 Dec 2026, with an online arrival card required from 1 Jan 2026; exemption beyond 2026 not yet announced. The Workation (F-1-D) visa lets remote workers employed abroad stay 1 year, extendable once (so 2 years in total), but needs income of about twice Korea's GNI per capita (about KRW 85-88 million, roughly USD 65,000), a year of experience in the same industry, medical cover of KRW 100 million, and background checks; apply at a consulate or switch from B-1/B-2/C-3 inside Korea. Tax residency generally begins at 183 days of presence.

events.name: Spring yellow dust and fine-dust season peaks (Mar-Apr)
Seollal (lunar new year) holiday, many shops shut for 3 days

locales.caveats: The workation visa was a pilot that reportedly went nationwide in July 2026 with eased rules; the official consulate page found is dated January 2024 and the 2026 details (threshold KRW 88.1 million, 1+1 years) come from secondary coverage, so confirm on hikorea.go.kr. Seoul's 2025 PM2.5 mean of 18 ug/m3 is from the city government via the Korea Times. Cost range rests on aggregator sites with wide spread and no Mapo officetel quote in EUR.

locales.name: Sri Lanka east coast
locales.area: Arugam Bay and Trincomalee; Trincomalee is the city in the data
locales.summary: Arugam Bay and Trincomalee are the quieter, cheaper half of Sri Lanka, at their best when the south coast is in monsoon, with surf, whales and long empty beaches. Infrastructure is thinner (patchy internet, basic hospitals, an 8-hour drive to Colombo) and the north-east monsoon makes November to January a poor time to be here.

monthNotes.reason: dry (about 30-80mm a month), sea breeze, Arugam Bay peak surf; 31-33C
mostly dry (about 50-100mm) but hot, 32-35C, with inter-monsoon thunderstorms in April
October inter-monsoon storms, about 220mm; February drying out but sea and weather still unsettled
NE monsoon peak: Trincomalee about 340mm in November and 370mm in December, floods and cyclone risk, boats and guesthouses shut

stay.why: May-September base; fewer services than the south, so pair with the south coast for the rest of the year

cost.note: basic furnished room or small house, food, scooter; Arugam Bay prices peak July-August; excludes insurance and visa fees

entry.summary: Digital Nomad Visa (launched Feb 2026): 1 year, renewable annually, USD 2,000/month foreign-sourced income remitted (+USD 500/month per dependant beyond 2), USD 500 per person per year, needs international health insurance, police clearance, medical and security clearance and a Ministry of Digital Economy recommendation; renewal requires Inland Revenue tax registration; no local employment. Without it: since 25 May 2026 EU/US/UK passport holders (most EU states, UK, USA, Canada, Australia on the list of 40) get a free 30-day double-entry tourist ETA, applied for before travel; extensions beyond 30 days cost a fee and reportedly run in steps to a 270-day maximum. Tax residency: a resident for tax if present 183+ days in a year, so a 270-day tourist stay can trigger it.

events.name: Whale and dolphin watching off Trincomalee (about Mar-Sep)

locales.caveats: Thin data: no monthly rainfall table found for Arugam Bay or Batticaloa (Trincomalee figures used; Pottuvil/Arugam Bay is a little drier). Air quality is an estimate with no station data. Cost and internet are estimated from the south-coast comparison and nomad forums; the nearest airport for visits is Batticaloa/Trincomalee domestic strips or CMB (7-9 h by road), and serious care means Colombo or Kandy. Cyclone Ditwah (Nov 2025) caused heavy rain and landslides in the eastern and central regions. DNV and ETA terms are the same as the south coast.
